dedupe_keys.name: catchment data explorer england water body status and river basin management plan data

description: The Catchment Data Explorer of the Environment Agency lets users explore and download the data behind England's river basin management plans. Data are organised in a hierarchy of 10 river basin districts, management catchments, operational catchments and water bodies, and for each water body give the status classifications (overall, ecological, chemical or quantitative status, broken into components and elements such as fish), site-level classifications, the reasons for not achieving good status, objectives with target dates, planned measures and protected areas, with boundaries for mapping. It offers a map and search interface, printable summary tables, an API, and national downloads as CSV, Shapefile and GeoJSON, all under the Open Government Licence without registration; the latest data were updated on 17 March 2025. Caveats: the national classification CSV is large, classification methods changed between cycles (for example chemical status in cycle 2), biota standards are not yet used for chemical status, and it covers England only. Simulation uses: linking wastewater discharges, storm overflows and abstractions to receiving water status, targeting treatment and drainage upgrades, catchment planning scenarios, and adding environmental constraints to water resource and supply models. Related records: Environment Agency storm overflow returns (data-ea-edm-storm-overflows-annual-returns).
